title: Zero-worker fleets cannot refresh the delivery health they need to dispatch
problem_statement: delivery_health evidence has a single evidence_ttl_seconds (default 300) cache lifetime and is otherwise entirely demand-driven: a lane is only re-probed when something in the current cycle asks for it. Two demand sources existed before this task: idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets, which refreshes only the exact owner/reviewer already recorded on the canonical task row, and unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets, which does walk the configured worker_reassignment fallback chains but only once the incumbent is durably (terminally) unavailable -- a merely stale/expired ('unknown') probe is not terminal, so it never triggers that walk. plan_task_assignment_pair and worker_recovery_assignment_pair both search the same fallback chains for a viable owner/reviewer pair. With a live worker running, some other cycle eventually re-touches each candidate lane and this self-heals. With zero active workers, nothing else ever does. This was reproduced live twice: a 13.6-hour zero-dispatch stall (2026-09-21T14:00Z to 2026-09-22T03:35Z) and a worker_recovery receipt stuck 'pending' for roughly 20 hours from 2026-09-22T04:44Z, both resolved only by an operator repeatedly driving 'supervisor.py --request-delivery-health-refresh' until a probe happened to land inside the 5-minute TTL window a retry also ran in.

revision_history.cut_1: ea39fdbfa9fb9c79251e6a62c7fccccdf8a1239f -- introduced zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets. Reviewer-side walk rooted only at the incumbent reviewer.
revision_history.cut_2_pr_5959: f4747870551b4b1dc0a0ea90918104aeaeac57dc -- made the reviewer-fallback walk reuse reviewer_fallback_search_order per candidate owner and seeded owner/reviewer walks from a pending receipt's previous owner/reviewer. Independently reviewed and REJECTED: still self-locked a plain ready-work, no-receipt case because (a) the owner-candidate scan excluded the incumbent reviewer, and (b) the reviewer-fallback-chain walk was gated behind ready_dispatch.review_statuses, which an ordinary todo/in_progress task never enters.
revision_history.cut_3_this_revision: Fixes both defects the review identified. See change_summary below.

supervisor_py.fix_1_owner_exclude: owner_exclude no longer includes the incumbent reviewer. Previously `owner_exclude = {owner, reviewer} | (lost_agent)` silently dropped the incumbent reviewer from the owner-candidate scan even when it is a configured owner fallback (for example owner_fallbacks Codex->[Codex2] with reviewer already Codex2). plan_task_assignment_pair (supervisor.py:5970) only ever excludes the incumbent owner itself when building owner_order (`reassignment_candidate_order(..., exclude={owner})`) -- its docstring states it 'never rejects an otherwise viable owner merely because that agent is the incumbent reviewer'. owner_exclude is now `{owner} | (lost_agent, when a pending receipt names one)`, matching the real planner exactly.
supervisor_py.fix_2_reviewer_chain_gating: The reviewer-fallback-chain walk (demand_refresh(reviewer) plus reviewer_fallback_search_order for the incumbent owner and every discovered owner candidate) previously ran only inside `if reviewer_side:`, and reviewer_side requires the task's own status to be in ready_dispatch.review_statuses (default just 'review') or the task to carry a pending worker-recovery receipt. An ordinary todo/in_progress task is neither, so the reviewer-pairing chain never ran for it at all -- even a correctly widened owner scan would have found a viable candidate owner with no reviewer ever demanded for it. The chain now runs whenever `(owner_side or reviewer_side)` and the reviewer is not an explicit Human/Ops gate, since plan_task_assignment_pair always needs this pairing the moment it considers any owner reassignment, independent of the task's own review-status gate. The pending-receipt-specific extra walk (seeded from a receipt's previous owner/reviewer, replacing the reviewer role itself) remains scoped to reviewer_side, since it is specific to worker_recovery_assignment_pair's reviewer-role search.
supervisor_py.no_change: _demand_endpoint_health_refresh, the shared health_gate_for_endpoint-backed probe-dedup helper, and the live_total==0 short-circuit are unchanged from cut 2.

test_supervisor_py.purpose: Reproduces the exact deterministic isolated repro from the independent review: zero workers, todo task owner Codex / reviewer Codex2, owner_fallbacks Codex->[Codex2], reviewer_fallbacks Codex2->[Claude], healthy Claude, codex-account retry_after/quota_terminal (far-future retry_at), codex2 endpoint expired. Asserts the demand scan returns exactly {codex2} (not [] as before the fix), that build_dispatch_plan folds it into health_refresh_targets, that a running fleet (live_total=1) adds nothing, and -- after simulating the demanded refresh landing -- that plan_task_assignment_pair now reaches the real planner's expected (Codex2, Claude) pair. This closes the loop from demand through to an actual viable dispatch pair, not just the refresh-target list.
test_supervisor_py.regression_fixed: test_idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets_filters_by_status_snapshot previously relied, incidentally, on the exact bug being fixed: its task used the default task_fixture reviewer (Codex2) with owner Codex under the default owner_fallbacks {Codex: [Codex2]}, so removing the incumbent-reviewer exclusion from the owner-candidate scan legitimately makes zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets start demanding codex2 for that task too (it is a genuine configured owner fallback). That test is about idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets's own narrower active-lane filtering, not about fallback-graph widening, so it was updated to clear worker_reassignment.owner_fallbacks/reviewer_fallbacks and use an explicit Human/Ops reviewer for its task, isolating it from the (now correctly firing) zero-fleet fallback scan without weakening what it actually asserts.

docs_operations_auto_worker_readiness_md.change: Extended the existing '### Delivery health refresh demand and the zero-worker self-lock' subsection with a new paragraph documenting the PR #5959 rejection, the two compounding defects, and the fix, in the same precise function/line-citation style as the rest of the section. Also updated the build_dispatch_plan / worker_recovery_assignment_pair line-number citations to match this revision's supervisor.py.

ac1_self_triggered_refresh_no_operator_c.criterion: a cycle that finds ready work or a pending worker recovery receipt while zero workers are active refreshes the delivery health it needs without any operator command
ac1_self_triggered_refresh_no_operator_c.evidence: test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_ready_work_no_receipt proves the exact case the review found unrecoverable: a plain todo task with an incumbent reviewer that is also the only owner fallback now correctly demands the stale candidate's endpoint (codex2) with no request_delivery_health_refresh set, and the pending-receipt cases from the prior revision (test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_pending_recovery_fallback, test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_candidate_owner_reviewer_chain) continue to pass unmodified.

ac2_stays_inside_probe_budget_never_prob.criterion: that self-triggered refresh stays inside the existing demand-driven probe budget and never probes providers that are already fresh
ac2_stays_inside_probe_budget_never_prob.evidence: No change to refresh_max_per_cycle or the shared health_gate_for_endpoint predicate. test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_skips_already_fresh_candidates (unmodified) and the healthy Claude endpoint inside the new no-receipt test (its account/endpoint stay healthy throughout and never appear in targets, even though it is walked as a reviewer-fallback candidate) both demonstrate an already-fresh lane produces no probe demand.

ac3_retry_and_refresh_ordered_same_cycle.criterion: the recovery retry and the refresh are ordered so the retry evaluates evidence that is still valid in the same cycle
ac3_retry_and_refresh_ordered_same_cycle.evidence: Unchanged from the prior revision: commit_delivery_health_observations commits this cycle's probed delivery_health before apply_post_dispatch_maintenance's reconcile_pending_worker_recoveries pass runs, and the new demand target is folded into the same cycle's probe_targets by build_dispatch_plan before probe_demanded_delivery_health runs. No phase reordering was needed or made in this revision either.

ac4_bounded_self_recovery.criterion: a fleet that reaches zero active workers with dispatchable work recovers on its own within a bounded number of cycles
ac4_bounded_self_recovery.evidence: test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_ready_work_no_receipt closes the loop end to end for the review's exact counterexample: after zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets demands the codex2 refresh and the simulated probe lands, plan_task_assignment_pair -- the real planner, called directly, not a mock -- returns (Codex2, Claude), proving the demanded refresh is sufficient for the actual dispatch decision to succeed on the very next evaluation, not just for a refresh-target list to be non-empty.

ac5_regression_tests.criterion: regression tests cover the zero-worker plus pending-receipt case and prove no extra probes are issued while workers are running
ac5_regression_tests.evidence: All five prior zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets tests pass unmodified, plus the new no-receipt test, which itself includes both a live_total=0 demand assertion and a live_total=1 no-extra-probes assertion (mirroring the existing pattern used by every other test in this group).

test_run_results.interpreter: .venv-pantheon/bin/python3 (Python 3.12, pytest 9.1.1; dependency interpreter inherited from the pre-provisioned worktree .venv-pantheon)

root_cause_analysis.why_owner_exclude_was_wrong: The zero-fleet scan's owner-candidate exclusion set was built by analogy to unavailable_assignment_fallback_refresh_targets's own `excluded = {owner, reviewer}`, but that sibling function only ever widens past the incumbent once assignment_terminal_unavailability(owner) is true -- a narrower, terminal-only trigger where excluding the reviewer too is comparatively low-cost (it will eventually get probed via the reviewer-status branch of the same function). zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets fires far more broadly (any dispatch-ready task, any status, purely on live_total==0), so the same reviewer exclusion silently starved the one candidate -- the incumbent reviewer -- that plan_task_assignment_pair explicitly permits as a replacement owner.
root_cause_analysis.why_reviewer_side_gating_was_wrong: reviewer_side exists to decide whether *this task's own* reviewer role needs replacing (task in review, or a pending receipt naming a lost reviewer). But the reviewer-fallback-chain walk added in cut 2 serves a different purpose entirely: pairing whichever *owner* the scan discovers with a reviewer that is not that same agent, exactly what plan_task_assignment_pair does for every candidate_owner it tries via reviewer_fallback_search_order. Conflating 'does this task need a new reviewer' with 'does this task's owner-reassignment search need reviewer pairing' meant the pairing chain silently no-opped for the entire todo/in_progress population, which is most of the fleet's normal working set.
root_cause_analysis.fix: Split the two concerns: owner_exclude now matches plan_task_assignment_pair's own exclusion set exactly ({owner} plus a receipt's lost agent), and the reviewer-pairing chain now runs whenever owner_side is true (in addition to reviewer_side), while the receipt-previous-owner/reviewer-seeded reviewer-role-replacement walk stays scoped to reviewer_side, since that part is genuinely specific to the reviewer role being lost.

review_notes_for_codex: This revision responds directly to the PR #5959 rejection (head f4747870551b4b1dc0a0ea90918104aeaeac57dc). Both P1 defects it identified are fixed: owner_exclude (supervisor.py near line 10885 in the rejected head) no longer includes the incumbent reviewer, and the reviewer-fallback-chain walk (previously gated at the `if reviewer_side:` near line 10896 in the rejected head) now also runs whenever owner_side is true.

New test test_zero_fleet_assignment_refresh_targets_covers_ready_work_no_receipt reproduces the review's own deterministic isolated repro verbatim (owner_fallbacks Codex->[Codex2], reviewer_fallbacks Codex2->[Claude], codex-account quota_terminal, codex2 endpoint expired, Claude healthy) and additionally calls plan_task_assignment_pair after simulating the refresh, proving the real planner reaches (Codex2, Claude) -- not just that a refresh target is produced.

test_idle_delivery_health_refresh_targets_filters_by_status_snapshot needed a small, scoped update (clear owner_fallbacks/reviewer_fallbacks, use an explicit Human/Ops reviewer for its task) because it was, without documenting so, relying on the exact bug this task fixes: its default-fixture task (owner Codex, reviewer Codex2) is itself a case where Codex2 is both the incumbent reviewer and Codex's only configured owner fallback. The update isolates the test to what it actually documents (idle-refresh active-lane filtering) rather than incidentally re-testing the fallback-widening bug.

AC3 required no further change in this revision; the same-cycle ordering argument from the prior evidence file still applies unchanged and was re-verified by reading the call sequence, not a new test.

Live production recovery (the two real stalls cited in the task brief) is not independently re-reproduced beyond the unit regression tests in this revision either -- this remains a supervisor-internal planning-logic fix verified at the unit level.
